Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

## PR Description

Closes #1734
### What changed
The resumed-context cache key now carries the resume parity budget as a build `variant`, so a warm-switch hit only serves a context built under the same budget.

### Key decisions
- `ResumedContextCache.match`/`remember` accept an optional `variant` (default `0`, backward compatible); a mismatch is a clean miss, not an eviction
- `session_commands.dart` computes the budget once before the cache probe and threads it into both `match` and `remember`
- Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context

```bash
dart test test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart   # 10 tests, incl. the new variant-miss case
```
Full `dart test`: 18 failures, all reproduced on `origin/main` (headless log/tools, backend-mode, yolo-rm, browser_ext e2e) — environment-dependent, no regressions from this change.

# gh-1734: [PERF] Session open: 6s cold boot / 12s via /sessions picker — double-paid boot, 2s context build, 4s shell boot

## Description

## Measurements (post-#1726/#1729, fa 1.0.615, goal_builder = 2.7GB JSONL)

The pathological opens are gone (was 31s+3.5min LM cap → now 70ms tail-read). What remains, measured from `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` boot_stage/resume_timing lines (2026-10-21):

**`fa --session goal_builder` — ~6s total:**
| stage | ms |
|---|---|
| session open (windowed tail-read of 2.7GB) | 70 |
| context build (estimator walk + pairing repair + image registry over the 200-record window) | ~2000 |
| process shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init | ~3500-4000 (unlogged remainder) |

**`fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder — ~12s total:** pays the ENTIRE boot stack twice — full shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (**1839ms** logged at 09:13:53) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

## Root causes (ranked by user-visible win)

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI. Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

## Acceptance

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

## PR Description

Closes #1734
### What changed
The resumed-context cache key now carries the resume parity budget as a build `variant`, so a warm-switch hit only serves a context built under the same budget.

### Key decisions
- `ResumedContextCache.match`/`remember` accept an optional `variant` (default `0`, backward compatible); a mismatch is a clean miss, not an eviction
- `session_commands.dart` computes the budget once before the cache probe and threads it into both `match` and `remember`
- Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart   # 10 tests, incl. the new variant-miss case
```
Full `dart test`: 18 failures, all reproduced on `origin/main` (headless log/tools, backend-mode, yolo-rm, browser_ext e2e) — environment-dependent, no regressions from this change.

# gh-1734: [PERF] Session open: 6s cold boot / 12s via /sessions picker — double-paid boot, 2s context build, 4s shell boot

## Description

## Measurements (post-#1726/#1729, fa 1.0.615, goal_builder = 2.7GB JSONL)

The pathological opens are gone (was 31s+3.5min LM cap → now 70ms tail-read). What remains, measured from `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` boot_stage/resume_timing lines (2026-10-21):

**`fa --session goal_builder` — ~6s total:**
| stage | ms |
|---|---|
| session open (windowed tail-read of 2.7GB) | 70 |
| context build (estimator walk + pairing repair + image registry over the 200-record window) | ~2000 |
| process shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init | ~3500-4000 (unlogged remainder) |

**`fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder — ~12s total:** pays the ENTIRE boot stack twice — full shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (**1839ms** logged at 09:13:53) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

## Root causes (ranked by user-visible win)

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI. Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

## Acceptance

- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s on this machine (2.7GB session)
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch to any session ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`
- no regression: over-window instant trim (#1726), lazy defer regime (#1729) keep their behavior + tests stay green

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
# Inline comment 1 — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the scan memo grows without bound across session paths

`lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:923`:

```dart
/// Per-path last-entry memo behind [readCustomRecordsOfType]; one entry
/// per session path bounds the memory (records are small, the newest
/// scan wins).
final Map<String, _CustomRecordScanMemo> _scanMemo = {};
```

One entry **per path** does not bound the map: the process's REPL/picker can
visit an unbounded number of distinct session paths, and entries are only
ever overwritten (same path) — never evicted. Every visited session leaves a
resident `_CustomRecordScanMemo` holding its full scan result (registry
snapshots, obligations, steering, orphan reports — potentially thousands of
records on a marathon session) for the process lifetime.

The sibling cache added by this same PR got exactly the right treatment —
`ResumedContextCache` is LRU-bounded (`capacity = 4`). The scan memo should
ride the same bound, e.g. the same remove/re-insert + `while (length >
capacity)` eviction pattern, so the two memo layers degrade consistently on
long picker-heavy sessions.

The immutability contract itself checks out — I verified all current callers
(`agent_cli_steering.dart:459`, `agent_cli_persist.dart:161`,
`child_session_io.dart:57`, `session_commands.dart:795`,

## PR Description

Closes #1734
### What changed
The resumed-context cache key now carries the resume parity budget as a build `variant`, so a warm-switch hit only serves a context built under the same budget.

### Key decisions
- `ResumedContextCache.match`/`remember` accept an optional `variant` (default `0`, backward compatible); a mismatch is a clean miss, not an eviction
- `session_commands.dart` computes the budget once before the cache probe and threads it into both `match` and `remember`
- Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart   # 10 tests, incl. the new variant-miss case
```
Full `dart test`: 18 failures, all reproduced on `origin/main` (headless log/tools, backend-mode, yolo-rm, browser_ext e2e) — environment-dependent, no regressions from this change.

# gh-1734: [PERF] Session open: 6s cold boot / 12s via /sessions picker — double-paid boot, 2s context build, 4s shell boot

## Description

## Measurements (post-#1726/#1729, fa 1.0.615, goal_builder = 2.7GB JSONL)

The pathological opens are gone (was 31s+3.5min LM cap → now 70ms tail-read). What remains, measured from `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` boot_stage/resume_timing lines (2026-10-21):

**`fa --session goal_builder` — ~6s total:**
| stage | ms |
|---|---|
| session open (windowed tail-read of 2.7GB) | 70 |
| context build (estimator walk + pairing repair + image registry over the 200-record window) | ~2000 |
| process shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init | ~3500-4000 (unlogged remainder) |

**`fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder — ~12s total:** pays the ENTIRE boot stack twice — full shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (**1839ms** logged at 09:13:53) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

## Root causes (ranked by user-visible win)

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI. Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

## Acceptance

- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s on this machine (2.7GB session)
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch to any session ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`
- no regression: over-window instant trim (#1726), lazy defer regime (#1729) keep their behavior + tests stay green

Related: #1728 (the switch lease race — same machinery; fixing the double-pay touches the same code and should land after/with it).

# Inline comment 1 — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the scan memo grows without bound across session paths

`lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:923`:

```dart
/// Per-path last-entry memo behind [readCustomRecordsOfType]; one entry
/// per session path bounds the memory (records are small, the newest
/// scan wins).
final Map<String, _CustomRecordScanMemo> _scanMemo = {};
```

One entry **per path** does not bound the map: the process's REPL/picker can
visit an unbounded number of distinct session paths, and entries are only
ever overwritten (same path) — never evicted. Every visited session leaves a
resident `_CustomRecordScanMemo` holding its full scan result (registry
snapshots, obligations, steering, orphan reports — potentially thousands of
records on a marathon session) for the process lifetime.

The sibling cache added by this same PR got exactly the right treatment —
`ResumedContextCache` is LRU-bounded (`capacity = 4`). The scan memo should
ride the same bound, e.g. the same remove/re-insert + `while (length >
capacity)` eviction pattern, so the two memo layers degrade consistently on
long picker-heavy sessions.

The immutability contract itself checks out — I verified all current callers
(`agent_cli_steering.dart:459`, `agent_cli_persist.dart:161`,
`child_session_io.dart:57`, `session_commands.dart:795`,

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

## PR Description

Closes #1734
### What changed
The resumed-context cache key now carries the resume parity budget as a build `variant`, so a warm-switch hit only serves a context built under the same budget.

### Key decisions
- `ResumedContextCache.match`/`remember` accept an optional `variant` (default `0`, backward compatible); a mismatch is a clean miss, not an eviction
- `session_commands.dart` computes the budget once before the cache probe and threads it into both `match` and `remember`
- Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart   # 10 tests, incl. the new variant-miss case
```
Full `dart test`: 18 failures, all reproduced on `origin/main` (headless log/tools, backend-mode, yolo-rm, browser_ext e2e) — environment-dependent, no regressions from this change.

# gh-1734: [PERF] Session open: 6s cold boot / 12s via /sessions picker — double-paid boot, 2s context build, 4s shell boot

## Description

## Measurements (post-#1726/#1729, fa 1.0.615, goal_builder = 2.7GB JSONL)

The pathological opens are gone (was 31s+3.5min LM cap → now 70ms tail-read). What remains, measured from `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` boot_stage/resume_timing lines (2026-10-21):

**`fa --session goal_builder` — ~6s total:**
| stage | ms |
|---|---|
| session open (windowed tail-read of 2.7GB) | 70 |
| context build (estimator walk + pairing repair + image registry over the 200-record window) | ~2000 |
| process shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init | ~3500-4000 (unlogged remainder) |

**`fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder — ~12s total:** pays the ENTIRE boot stack twice — full shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (**1839ms** logged at 09:13:53) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

## Root causes (ranked by user-visible win)

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI. Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

## Acceptance

- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s on this machine (2.7GB session)
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch to any session ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`

One entry **per path** does not bound the map: the process's REPL/picker can

ride the same bound, e.g. the same remove/re-insert + `while (length >

long picker-heavy sessions.

pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #1734
### What changed
The resumed-context cache key now carries the resume parity budget as a build `variant`, so a warm-switch hit only serves a context built under the same budget.

### Key decisions
- `ResumedContextCache.match`/`remember` accept an optional `variant` (default `0`, backward compatible); a mismatch is a clean miss, not an eviction
- `session_commands.dart` computes the budget once before the cache probe and threads it into both `match` and `remember`
- Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart   # 10 tests, incl. the new variant-miss case
```
Full `dart test`: 18 failures, all reproduced on `origin/main` (headless log/tools, backend-mode, yolo-rm, browser_ext e2e) — environment-dependent, no regressions from this change.

# gh-1734: [PERF] Session open: 6s cold boot / 12s via /sessions picker — double-paid boot, 2s context build, 4s shell boot

## Description

## Measurements (post-#1726/#1729, fa 1.0.615, goal_builder = 2.7GB JSONL)

The pathological opens are gone (was 31s+3.5min LM cap → now 70ms tail-read). What remains, measured from `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` boot_stage/resume_timing lines (2026-10-21):

**`fa --session goal_builder` — ~6s total:**
| stage | ms |
|---|---|
| session open (windowed tail-read of 2.7GB) | 70 |
| context build (estimator walk + pairing repair + image registry over the 200-record window) | ~2000 |
| process shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init | ~3500-4000 (unlogged remainder) |

**`fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder — ~12s total:** pays the ENTIRE boot stack twice — full shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (**1839ms** logged at 09:13:53) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

## Root causes (ranked by user-visible win)

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI. Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

## Acceptance

- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s on this machine (2.7GB session)
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch to any session ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`
- no regression: over-window instant trim (#1726), lazy defer regime (#1729) keep their behavior + tests stay green

Related: #1728 (the switch lease race — same machinery; fixing the double-pay touches the same code and should land after/with it).

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
# Inline comment 1 — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the scan memo grows without bound across session paths

`lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:923`:

```dart
/// Per-path last-entry memo behind [readCustomRecordsOfType]; one entry
/// per session path bounds the memory (records are small, the newest
/// scan wins).
final Map<String, _CustomRecordScanMemo> _scanMemo = {};
```

One entry **per path** does not bound the map: the process's REPL/picker can
visit an unbounded number of distinct session paths, and entries are only
ever overwritten (same path) — never evicted. Every visited session leaves a
resident `_CustomRecordScanMemo` holding its full scan result (registry
snapshots, obligations, steering, orphan reports — potentially thousands of
records on a marathon session) for the process lifetime.

The sibling cache added by this same PR got exactly the right treatment —
`ResumedContextCache` is LRU-bounded (`capacity = 4`). The scan memo should
ride the same bound, e.g. the same remove/re-insert + `while (length >
capacity)` eviction pattern, so the two memo layers degrade consistently on
long picker-heavy sessions.

The immutability contract itself checks out — I verified all current callers
(`agent_cli_steering.dart:459`, `agent_cli_persist.dart:161`,
`child_session_io.dart:57`, `session_commands.dart:795`,

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## PR Description

Closes #1734
### What changed
The resumed-context cache key now carries the resume parity budget as a build `variant`, so a warm-switch hit only serves a context built under the same budget.

### Key decisions
- `ResumedContextCache.match`/`remember` accept an optional `variant` (default `0`, backward compatible); a mismatch is a clean miss, not an eviction
- `session_commands.dart` computes the budget once before the cache probe and threads it into both `match` and `remember`
- Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart   # 10 tests, incl. the new variant-miss case
```
Full `dart test`: 18 failures, all reproduced on `origin/main` (headless log/tools, backend-mode, yolo-rm, browser_ext e2e) — environment-dependent, no regressions from this change.

# gh-1734: [PERF] Session open: 6s cold boot / 12s via /sessions picker — double-paid boot, 2s context build, 4s shell boot

## Description

## Measurements (post-#1726/#1729, fa 1.0.615, goal_builder = 2.7GB JSONL)

The pathological opens are gone (was 31s+3.5min LM cap → now 70ms tail-read). What remains, measured from `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` boot_stage/resume_timing lines (2026-10-21):

**`fa --session goal_builder` — ~6s total:**
| stage | ms |
|---|---|
| session open (windowed tail-read of 2.7GB) | 70 |
| context build (estimator walk + pairing repair + image registry over the 200-record window) | ~2000 |
| process shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init | ~3500-4000 (unlogged remainder) |

**`fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder — ~12s total:** pays the ENTIRE boot stack twice — full shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (**1839ms** logged at 09:13:53) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

## Root causes (ranked by user-visible win)

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI. Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

## Acceptance

- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s on this machine (2.7GB session)
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch to any session ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`

# PR Discussion History

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 1 — `lib/src/session/session_repo.dart` line 923

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
# Inline comment 1 — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the scan memo grows without bound across session paths

`lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:923`:

```dart
/// Per-path last-entry memo behind [readCustomRecordsOfType]; one entry
/// per session path bounds the memory (records are small, the newest
/// scan wins).
final Map<String, _CustomRecordScanMemo> _scanMemo = {};
```

One entry **per path** does not bound the map: the process's REPL/picker can
visit an unbounded number of distinct session paths, and entries are only
ever overwritten (same path) — never evicted. Every visited session leaves a
resident `_CustomRecordScanMemo` holding its full scan result (registry
snapshots, obligations, steering, orphan reports — potentially thousands of
records on a marathon session) for the process lifetime.

The sibling cache added by this same PR got exactly the right treatment —
`ResumedContextCache` is LRU-bounded (`capacity = 4`). The scan memo should
ride the same bound, e.g. the same remove/re-insert + `while (length >
capacity)` eviction pattern, so the two memo layers degrade consistently on
long picker-heavy sessions.

The immutability contract itself checks out — I verified all current callers
(`agent_cli_steering.dart:459`, `agent_cli_persist.dart:161`,

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. ## PR Description

Closes #1734
### What changed
The resumed-context cache key now carries the resume parity budget as a build `variant`, so a warm-switch hit only serves a context built under the same budget.

### Key decisions
- `ResumedContextCache.match`/`remember` accept an optional `variant` (default `0`, backward compatible); a mismatch is a clean miss, not an eviction
- `session_commands.dart` computes the budget once before the cache probe and threads it into both `match` and `remember`
- Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart   # 10 tests, incl. the new variant-miss case
```
Full `dart test`: 18 failures, all reproduced on `origin/main` (headless log/tools, backend-mode, yolo-rm, browser_ext e2e) — environment-dependent, no regressions from this change.

# gh-1734: [PERF] Session open: 6s cold boot / 12s via /sessions picker — double-paid boot, 2s context build, 4s shell boot

## Description

## Measurements (post-#1726/#1729, fa 1.0.615, goal_builder = 2.7GB JSONL)

The pathological opens are gone (was 31s+3.5min LM cap → now 70ms tail-read). What remains, measured from `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` boot_stage/resume_timing lines (2026-10-21):

**`fa --session goal_builder` — ~6s total:**
| stage | ms |
|---|---|
| session open (windowed tail-read of 2.7GB) | 70 |
| context build (estimator walk + pairing repair + image registry over the 200-record window) | ~2000 |
| process shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init | ~3500-4000 (unlogged remainder) |

**`fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder — ~12s total:** pays the ENTIRE boot stack twice — full shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (**1839ms** logged at 09:13:53) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

## Root causes (ranked by user-visible win)

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI. Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

## Acceptance

- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s on this machine (2.7GB session)
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch to any session ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`
- no regression: over-window instant trim (#1726), lazy defer regime (#1729) keep their behavior + tests stay green

long picker-heavy sessions.

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` …

## PR Description

Closes #1734
### What changed
The resumed-context cache key now carries the resume parity budget as a build `variant`, so a warm-switch hit only serves a context built under the same budget.

### Key decisions
- `ResumedContextCache.match`/`remember` accept an optional `variant` (default `0`, backward compatible); a mismatch is a clean miss, not an eviction
- `session_commands.dart` computes the budget once before the cache probe and threads it into both `match` and `remember`
- Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart   # 10 tests, incl. the new variant-miss case
```
Full `dart test`: 18 failures, all reproduced on `origin/main` (headless log/tools, backend-mode, yolo-rm, browser_ext e2e) — environment-dependent, no regressions from this change.

# gh-1734: [PERF] Session open: 6s cold boot / 12s via /sessions picker — double-paid boot, 2s context build, 4s shell boot

## Description

## Measurements (post-#1726/#1729, fa 1.0.615, goal_builder = 2.7GB JSONL)

The pathological opens are gone (was 31s+3.5min LM cap → now 70ms tail-read). What remains, measured from `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` boot_stage/resume_timing lines (2026-10-21):

**`fa --session goal_builder` — ~6s total:**
| stage | ms |
|---|---|
| session open (windowed tail-read of 2.7GB) | 70 |
| context build (estimator walk + pairing repair + image registry over the 200-record window) | ~2000 |
| process shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init | ~3500-4000 (unlogged remainder) |

**`fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder — ~12s total:** pays the ENTIRE boot stack twice — full shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (**1839ms** logged at 09:13:53) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

## Root causes (ranked by user-visible win)

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI. Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

## Acceptance

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
# Inline comment 1 — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the scan memo grows without bound across session paths

`lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:923`:

```dart
/// Per-path last-entry memo behind [readCustomRecordsOfType]; one entry
/// per session path bounds the memory (records are small, the newest
/// scan wins).
final Map<String, _CustomRecordScanMemo> _scanMemo = {};
```

One entry **per path** does not bound the map: the process's REPL/picker can
visit an unbounded number of distinct session paths, and entries are only
ever overwritten (same path) — never evicted. Every visited session leaves a
resident `_CustomRecordScanMemo` holding its full scan result (registry
snapshots, obligations, steering, orphan reports — potentially thousands of
records on a marathon session) for the process lifetime.

The sibling cache added by this same PR got exactly the right treatment —
`ResumedContextCache` is LRU-bounded (`capacity = 4`). The scan memo should
ride the same bound, e.g. the same remove/re-insert + `while (length >
capacity)` eviction pattern, so the two memo layers degrade consistently on
long picker-heavy sessions.

The immutability contract itself checks out — I verified all current callers
(`agent_cli_steering.dart:459`, `agent_cli_persist.dart:161`,
`child_session_io.dart:57`, `session_commands.dart:795`,
