Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (live: a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source did not contain — the reviewed code was behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. ## PR Description

Closes #1734
### What changed
The resumed-context cache key now carries the resume parity budget as a build `variant`, so a warm-switch hit only serves a context built under the same budget.

### Key decisions
- `ResumedContextCache.match`/`remember` accept an optional `variant` (default `0`, backward compatible); a mismatch is a clean miss, not an eviction
- `session_commands.dart` computes the budget once before the cache probe and threads it into both `match` and `remember`
- Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart   # 10 tests, incl. the new variant-miss case
```
Full `dart test`: 18 failures, all reproduced on `origin/main` (headless log/tools, backend-mode, yolo-rm, browser_ext e2e) — environment-dependent, no regressions from this change.

# gh-1734: [PERF] Session open: 6s cold boot / 12s via /sessions picker — double-paid boot, 2s context build, 4s shell boot

## Description

## Measurements (post-#1726/#1729, fa 1.0.615, goal_builder = 2.7GB JSONL)

The pathological opens are gone (was 31s+3.5min LM cap → now 70ms tail-read). What remains, measured from `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` boot_stage/resume_timing lines (2026-10-21):

**`fa --session goal_builder` — ~6s total:**
| stage | ms |
|---|---|
| session open (windowed tail-read of 2.7GB) | 70 |
| context build (estimator walk + pairing repair + image registry over the 200-record window) | ~2000 |
| process shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init | ~3500-4000 (unlogged remainder) |

**`fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder — ~12s total:** pays the ENTIRE boot stack twice — full shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (**1839ms** logged at 09:13:53) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

## Root causes (ranked by user-visible win)

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI. Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

## Acceptance

- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s on this machine (2.7GB session)
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch to any session ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`
- no regression: over-window instant trim (#1726), lazy defer regime (#1729) keep their behavior + tests stay green

Related: #1728 (the switch lease race — same machinery; fixing the double-pay touches the same code and should land after/with it).

records on a marathon session) for the process lifetime.

capacity)` eviction pattern, so the two memo layers degrade consistently on
long picker-heavy sessions.

blocks.text:
`resetLoadedUsageAnchors` is non-mutating — it uses `copyWith` to create new instances for assistant messages with usage, and passes everything else through as the same instance.

Now, the key correctness question: after the cached context is served, the messages (SHARED instances with the cache) get assigned to `_agent.state.messages`. During the live session, does the agent mutate Message objects in place, or does it create new ones? If the live loop mutates a message object in place (e.g., updating usage at generation time on the last assistant message), the cache's copy would be corrupted.

Note: `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` copies assistant messages with non-zero usage. On the FIRST load (fresh build), messages come from `buildContext()` — those instances get remembered in the cache via `remember(context: built)`. Wait — careful: the cache stores `built` (the original context). `match()` creates a NEW SessionContext with a fresh list but SHARED message instances.

Scenario: session S is opened at boot (fresh build) → context C1 built; messages M1..Mn are stored in cache AND used by the live agent (the same instances — `context.messages` list is used directly: `_agent.state.messages = resetLoadedUsageAnchors(messages)` — note resetLoadedUsageAnchors creates a NEW list, and copies assistant messages with usage != 0, but other messages pass through as the same instances).

So the live agent state may hold SOME of the same Message instances that the cache holds. Then user runs a prompt → does the agent mutate the last assistant message in place (stamp usage)? The doc of `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` says "the first live turn stamps fresh usage again" — how? If it mutates the AssistantMessage in place, the cached instance is mutated too.

Then a warm switch back to S (file unchanged — the file only changes when a record is appended; during the live session on ANOTHER session, S's file doesn't change) → `match()` returns the cached context with the (possibly mutated) message instances. If the live loop stamped usage into the shared instances... but wait — the live session was on a DIFFERENT session (beta), not S (alpha). The switch loaded beta's context and REPLACED `_agent.state.messages` with beta's messages. Alpha's message instances are no longer referenced by the live agent — unless the live loop held aliases (e.g., a tool result referencing a message object).

BUT: consider the SAME session being switched away and back where the live agent mutated messages BEFORE the switch... no wait, the cache entry is only remembered at build time (fresh from disk, unmutated), and `match` shares those instances. The risk is: hit 1 serves shared instances → live agent mutates instance X in place during its run → user switches away and back (file unchanged) → hit 2 serves the mutated X. If mutation is semantic (usage anchors — which get reset anyway by resetLoadedUsageAnchors on every load), it may benign. But other in-place mutations (ids, tool results, content) would corrupt.

Let me check how the agent appends/stamps messages. Search for in-place mutations of Message fields. The message classes — let me look at their definitions to see if fields are final.

The live loop can't mutate message objects in place; it can only replace them in lists (e.g., partial streaming replaces the message instance). # Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-1636): auto-compaction stops dumping the internal checkpoint
  summary into the console — the default report is ONE marker line
  (`● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`); the records
  line + fenced summary moved behind the new `tui.showCompactionDetails`
  opt-in (default false), and the manual `/compact` still prints the full
  block. The headless log face no longer streams the summarizer deltas by
  default (the gh-1433 E4 live stream is part of the same opt-in; the
  gh-1430 `… reasoning` liveness line still covers the window). Nothing
  is lost — the summary stays in the session file, reachable via
  `compact_expand`.

- fix(test): gh-1732 — the `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test` sustained-contention
  validation leg spikes 3 of the 5 doubled runs per attempt instead of 4
  (CI run 39546301132, core shard 2/4: the old shape left exactly ONE
  real-wall-clock-timed doubled sample per attempt, and real jitter on
  that single sample — the very shape being modeled — inflated all three
  attempts' min ratios to a 3.30x best against the 3.2 bound while the
  real 500k growth legs on the same runner stayed green). 3-of-5 is the
  documented live-red shape ("≥3 of the 5 timed runs"): median-of-5
  [c,c,s] is still a spiked value, so the leg still proves the
  pre-gh-1532 median harness fails, and the min harness now rides two
  clean doubled samples per attempt.

- fix(#1705): CLI fresh-install boarding asks the provider choice FIRST —
  the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (presets, `Custom` last) —

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert ## agent_task_preamble.md You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## general_guidelines.md # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. ## PR Description

Closes #1734
### What changed
The resumed-context cache key now carries the resume parity budget as a build `variant`, so a warm-switch hit only serves a context built under the same budget.

### Key decisions
- `ResumedContextCache.match`/`remember` accept an optional `variant` (default `0`, backward compatible); a mismatch is a clean miss, not an eviction
- `session_commands.dart` computes the budget once before the cache probe and threads it into both `match` and `remember`
- Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart   # 10 tests, incl. the new variant-miss case
```
Full `dart test`: 18 failures, all reproduced on `origin/main` (headless log/tools, backend-mode, yolo-rm, browser_ext e2e) — environment-dependent, no regressions from this change.

# gh-1734: [PERF] Session open: 6s cold boot / 12s via /sessions picker — double-paid boot, 2s context build, 4s shell boot

## Description

## Measurements (post-#1726/#1729, fa 1.0.615, goal_builder = 2.7GB JSONL)

The pathological opens are gone (was 31s+3.5min LM cap → now 70ms tail-read). What remains, measured from `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` boot_stage/resume_timing lines (2026-10-21):

**`fa --session goal_builder` — ~6s total:**
| stage | ms |
|---|---|
| session open (windowed tail-read of 2.7GB) | 70 |
| context build (estimator walk + pairing repair + image registry over the 200-record window) | ~2000 |
| process shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init | ~3500-4000 (unlogged remainder) |

**`fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder — ~12s total:** pays the ENTIRE boot stack twice — full shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (**1839ms** logged at 09:13:53) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

## Root causes (ranked by user-visible win)

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI. Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

## Acceptance

- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s on this machine (2.7GB session)
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch to any session ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`
- no regression: over-window instant trim (#1726), lazy defer regime (#1729) keep their behavior + tests stay green

long picker-heavy sessions.

messages.preview: `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` is copy-on-write, non-mutating. Now the critical shared-mutability question — are `Message` objects mutated in place by the live loop?

blocks.text:
`resetLoadedUsageAnchors` is non-mutating — it uses `copyWith` to create new instances for assistant messages with usage, and passes everything else through as the same instance.

Now, the key correctness question: after the cached context is served, the messages (SHARED instances with the cache) get assigned to `_agent.state.messages`. During the live session, does the agent mutate Message objects in place, or does it create new ones? If the live loop mutates a message object in place (e.g., updating usage at generation time on the last assistant message), the cache's copy would be corrupted.

Note: `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` copies assistant messages with non-zero usage. On the FIRST load (fresh build), messages come from `buildContext()` — those instances get remembered in the cache via `remember(context: built)`. Wait — careful: the cache stores `built` (the original context). `match()` creates a NEW SessionContext with a fresh list but SHARED message instances.

Scenario: session S is opened at boot (fresh build) → context C1 built; messages M1..Mn are stored in cache AND used by the live agent (the same instances — `context.messages` list is used directly: `_agent.state.messages = resetLoadedUsageAnchors(messages)` — note resetLoadedUsageAnchors creates a NEW list, and copies assistant messages with usage != 0, but other messages pass through as the same instances).

So the live agent state may hold SOME of the same Message instances that the cache holds. Then user runs a prompt → does the agent mutate the last assistant message in place (stamp usage)? The doc of `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` says "the first live turn stamps fresh usage again" — how? If it mutates the AssistantMessage in place, the cached instance is mutated too.

Then a warm switch back to S (file unchanged — the file only changes when a record is appended; during the live session on ANOTHER session, S's file doesn't change) → `match()` returns the cached context with the (possibly mutated) message instances. If the live loop stamped usage into the shared instances... but wait — the live session was on a DIFFERENT session (beta), not S (alpha). The switch loaded beta's context and REPLACED `_agent.state.messages` with beta's messages. Alpha's message instances are no longer referenced by the live agent — unless the live loop held aliases (e.g., a tool result referencing a message object).

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-1636): auto-compaction stops dumping the internal checkpoint
  summary into the console — the default report is ONE marker line
  (`● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`); the records
  line + fenced summary moved behind the new `tui.showCompactionDetails`
  opt-in (default false), and the manual `/compact` still prints the full
  block. The headless log face no longer streams the summarizer deltas by
  default (the gh-1433 E4 live stream is part of the same opt-in; the
  gh-1430 `… reasoning` liveness line still covers the window). Nothing
  is lost — the summary stays in the session file, reachable via
  `compact_expand`.

  validation leg spikes 3 of the 5 doubled runs per attempt instead of 4
  (CI run 39546301132, core shard 2/4: the old shape left exactly ONE
  real-wall-clock-timed doubled sample per attempt, and real jitter on
  that single sample — the very shape being modeled — inflated all three
  attempts' min ratios to a 3.30x best against the 3.2 bound while the
  real 500k growth legs on the same runner stayed green). 3-of-5 is the
  documented live-red shape ("≥3 of the 5 timed runs"): median-of-5
  [c,c,s] is still a spiked value, so the leg still proves the
  pre-gh-1532 median harness fails, and the min harness now rides two
  clean doubled samples per attempt.

## PR Description

Closes #1734
### What changed
The resumed-context cache key now carries the resume parity budget as a build `variant`, so a warm-switch hit only serves a context built under the same budget.

### Key decisions
- `ResumedContextCache.match`/`remember` accept an optional `variant` (default `0`, backward compatible); a mismatch is a clean miss, not an eviction
- `session_commands.dart` computes the budget once before the cache probe and threads it into both `match` and `remember`
- Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart   # 10 tests, incl. the new variant-miss case
```
Full `dart test`: 18 failures, all reproduced on `origin/main` (headless log/tools, backend-mode, yolo-rm, browser_ext e2e) — environment-dependent, no regressions from this change.

# gh-1734: [PERF] Session open: 6s cold boot / 12s via /sessions picker — double-paid boot, 2s context build, 4s shell boot

## Description

## Measurements (post-#1726/#1729, fa 1.0.615, goal_builder = 2.7GB JSONL)

The pathological opens are gone (was 31s+3.5min LM cap → now 70ms tail-read). What remains, measured from `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` boot_stage/resume_timing lines (2026-10-21):

**`fa --session goal_builder` — ~6s total:**
| stage | ms |
|---|---|
| session open (windowed tail-read of 2.7GB) | 70 |
| context build (estimator walk + pairing repair + image registry over the 200-record window) | ~2000 |
| process shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init | ~3500-4000 (unlogged remainder) |

**`fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder — ~12s total:** pays the ENTIRE boot stack twice — full shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (**1839ms** logged at 09:13:53) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

## Root causes (ranked by user-visible win)

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI. Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

## Acceptance

- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s on this machine (2.7GB session)
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch to any session ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`
- no regression: over-window instant trim (#1726), lazy defer regime (#1729) keep their behavior + tests stay green

On the FIRST load (fresh build), messages come from `buildContext()` — those instances get remembered in the cache via `remember(context: built)`. # Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-1636): auto-compaction stops dumping the internal checkpoint
  summary into the console — the default report is ONE marker line
  (`● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`); the records
  line + fenced summary moved behind the new `tui.showCompactionDetails`
  opt-in (default false), and the manual `/compact` still prints the full
  block. The headless log face no longer streams the summarizer deltas by
  default (the gh-1433 E4 live stream is part of the same opt-in; the
  gh-1430 `… reasoning` liveness line still covers the window). Nothing
  is lost — the summary stays in the session file, reachable via
  `compact_expand`.

- fix(test): gh-1732 — the `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test` sustained-contention
  validation leg spikes 3 of the 5 doubled runs per attempt instead of 4
  (CI run 39546301132, core shard 2/4: the old shape left exactly ONE
  real-wall-clock-timed doubled sample per attempt, and real jitter on
  that single sample — the very shape being modeled — inflated all three
  attempts' min ratios to a 3.30x best against the 3.2 bound while the
  real 500k growth legs on the same runner stayed green). 3-of-5 is the
  documented live-red shape ("≥3 of the 5 timed runs"): median-of-5
  [c,c,s] is still a spiked value, so the leg still proves the
  pre-gh-1532 median harness fails, and the min harness now rides two

## PR Description

Closes #1734
### What changed
The resumed-context cache key now carries the resume parity budget as a build `variant`, so a warm-switch hit only serves a context built under the same budget.

### Key decisions
- `ResumedContextCache.match`/`remember` accept an optional `variant` (default `0`, backward compatible); a mismatch is a clean miss, not an eviction
- `session_commands.dart` computes the budget once before the cache probe and threads it into both `match` and `remember`
- Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart   # 10 tests, incl. the new variant-miss case
```
Full `dart test`: 18 failures, all reproduced on `origin/main` (headless log/tools, backend-mode, yolo-rm, browser_ext e2e) — environment-dependent, no regressions from this change.

# gh-1734: [PERF] Session open: 6s cold boot / 12s via /sessions picker — double-paid boot, 2s context build, 4s shell boot

## Description

## Measurements (post-#1726/#1729, fa 1.0.615, goal_builder = 2.7GB JSONL)

The pathological opens are gone (was 31s+3.5min LM cap → now 70ms tail-read). What remains, measured from `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` boot_stage/resume_timing lines (2026-10-21):

**`fa --session goal_builder` — ~6s total:**
| stage | ms |
|---|---|
| session open (windowed tail-read of 2.7GB) | 70 |
| context build (estimator walk + pairing repair + image registry over the 200-record window) | ~2000 |
| process shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init | ~3500-4000 (unlogged remainder) |

**`fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder — ~12s total:** pays the ENTIRE boot stack twice — full shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (**1839ms** logged at 09:13:53) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

## Root causes (ranked by user-visible win)

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI. Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

## Acceptance

- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s on this machine (2.7GB session)
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch to any session ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`
- no regression: over-window instant trim (#1726), lazy defer regime (#1729) keep their behavior + tests stay green

Related: #1728 (the switch lease race — same machinery; fixing the double-pay touches the same code and should land after/with it).

blocks.text:
`resetLoadedUsageAnchors` is non-mutating — it uses `copyWith` to create new instances for assistant messages with usage, and passes everything else through as the same instance.

Now, the key correctness question: after the cached context is served, the messages (SHARED instances with the cache) get assigned to `_agent.state.messages`. During the live session, does the agent mutate Message objects in place, or does it create new ones? If the live loop mutates a message object in place (e.g., updating usage at generation time on the last assistant message), the cache's copy would be corrupted.

Note: `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` copies assistant messages with non-zero usage. On the FIRST load (fresh build), messages come from `buildContext()` — those instances get remembered in the cache via `remember(context: built)`. Wait — careful: the cache stores `built` (the original context). `match()` creates a NEW SessionContext with a fresh list but SHARED message instances.

Scenario: session S is opened at boot (fresh build) → context C1 built; messages M1..Mn are stored in cache AND used by the live agent (the same instances — `context.messages` list is used directly: `_agent.state.messages = resetLoadedUsageAnchors(messages)` — note resetLoadedUsageAnchors creates a NEW list, and copies assistant messages with usage != 0, but other messages pass through as the same instances).

So the live agent state may hold SOME of the same Message instances that the cache holds. Then user runs a prompt → does the agent mutate the last assistant message in place (stamp usage)? The doc of `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` says "the first live turn stamps fresh usage again" — how? If it mutates the AssistantMessage in place, the cached instance is mutated too.

Then a warm switch back to S (file unchanged — the file only changes when a record is appended; during the live session on ANOTHER session, S's file doesn't change) → `match()` returns the cached context with the (possibly mutated) message instances. If the live loop stamped usage into the shared instances... but wait — the live session was on a DIFFERENT session (beta), not S (alpha). The switch loaded beta's context and REPLACED `_agent.state.messages` with beta's messages. Alpha's message instances are no longer referenced by the live agent — unless the live loop held aliases (e.g., a tool result referencing a message object).

BUT: consider the SAME session being switched away and back where the live agent mutated messages BEFORE the switch... no wait, the cache entry is only remembered at build time (fresh from disk, unmutated), and `match` shares those instances. The risk is: hit 1 serves shared instances → live agent mutates instance X in place during its run → user switches away and back (file unchanged) → hit 2 serves the mutated X. If mutation is semantic (usage anchors — which get reset anyway by resetLoadedUsageAnchors on every load), it may benign. But other in-place mutations (ids, tool results, content) would corrupt.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## PR Description

Closes #1734
### What changed
The resumed-context cache key now carries the resume parity budget as a build `variant`, so a warm-switch hit only serves a context built under the same budget.

### Key decisions
- `ResumedContextCache.match`/`remember` accept an optional `variant` (default `0`, backward compatible); a mismatch is a clean miss, not an eviction
- `session_commands.dart` computes the budget once before the cache probe and threads it into both `match` and `remember`
- Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart   # 10 tests, incl. the new variant-miss case
```
Full `dart test`: 18 failures, all reproduced on `origin/main` (headless log/tools, backend-mode, yolo-rm, browser_ext e2e) — environment-dependent, no regressions from this change.

# gh-1734: [PERF] Session open: 6s cold boot / 12s via /sessions picker — double-paid boot, 2s context build, 4s shell boot

## Description

## Measurements (post-#1726/#1729, fa 1.0.615, goal_builder = 2.7GB JSONL)

The pathological opens are gone (was 31s+3.5min LM cap → now 70ms tail-read). What remains, measured from `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` boot_stage/resume_timing lines (2026-10-21):

**`fa --session goal_builder` — ~6s total:**
| stage | ms |
|---|---|
| session open (windowed tail-read of 2.7GB) | 70 |
| context build (estimator walk + pairing repair + image registry over the 200-record window) | ~2000 |
| process shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init | ~3500-4000 (unlogged remainder) |

**`fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder — ~12s total:** pays the ENTIRE boot stack twice — full shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (**1839ms** logged at 09:13:53) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

## Root causes (ranked by user-visible win)

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI. Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

## Acceptance

- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s on this machine (2.7GB session)
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch to any session ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`
- no regression: over-window instant trim (#1726), lazy defer regime (#1729) keep their behavior + tests stay green

Related: #1728 (the switch lease race — same machinery; fixing the double-pay touches the same code and should land after/with it).

# Inline comment 1 — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the scan memo grows without bound across session paths

`lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:923`:

```dart
/// Per-path last-entry memo behind [readCustomRecordsOfType]; one entry
/// per session path bounds the memory (records are small, the newest
/// scan wins).
final Map<String, _CustomRecordScanMemo> _scanMemo = {};
```

One entry **per path** does not bound the map: the process's REPL/picker can
visit an unbounded number of distinct session paths, and entries are only
ever overwritten (same path) — never evicted. Every visited session leaves a
resident `_CustomRecordScanMemo` holding its full scan result (registry
snapshots, obligations, steering, orphan reports — potentially thousands of
records on a marathon session) for the process lifetime.

The sibling cache added by this same PR got exactly the right treatment —
`ResumedContextCache` is LRU-bounded (`capacity = 4`). The scan memo should
ride the same bound, e.g. the same remove/re-insert + `while (length >
capacity)` eviction pattern, so the two memo layers degrade consistently on
long picker-heavy sessions.

`child_session_io.dart:57`, `session_commands.dart:795`,

blocks.text:
`resetLoadedUsageAnchors` is non-mutating — it uses `copyWith` to create new instances for assistant messages with usage, and passes everything else through as the same instance.

Now, the key correctness question: after the cached context is served, the messages (SHARED instances with the cache) get assigned to `_agent.state.messages`. During the live session, does the agent mutate Message objects in place, or does it create new ones? If the live loop mutates a message object in place (e.g., updating usage at generation time on the last assistant message), the cache's copy would be corrupted.

Note: `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` copies assistant messages with non-zero usage. On the FIRST load (fresh build), messages come from `buildContext()` — those instances get remembered in the cache via `remember(context: built)`. Wait — careful: the cache stores `built` (the original context). `match()` creates a NEW SessionContext with a fresh list but SHARED message instances.

Scenario: session S is opened at boot (fresh build) → context C1 built; messages M1..Mn are stored in cache AND used by the live agent (the same instances — `context.messages` list is used directly: `_agent.state.messages = resetLoadedUsageAnchors(messages)` — note resetLoadedUsageAnchors creates a NEW list, and copies assistant messages with usage != 0, but other messages pass through as the same instances).

So the live agent state may hold SOME of the same Message instances that the cache holds. Then user runs a prompt → does the agent mutate the last assistant message in place (stamp usage)? The doc of `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` says "the first live turn stamps fresh usage again" — how? If it mutates the AssistantMessage in place, the cached instance is mutated too.

Then a warm switch back to S (file unchanged — the file only changes when a record is appended; during the live session on ANOTHER session, S's file doesn't change) → `match()` returns the cached context with the (possibly mutated) message instances. If the live loop stamped usage into the shared instances... but wait — the live session was on a DIFFERENT session (beta), not S (alpha). The switch loaded beta's context and REPLACED `_agent.state.messages` with beta's messages. Alpha's message instances are no longer referenced by the live agent — unless the live loop held aliases (e.g., a tool result referencing a message object).

BUT: consider the SAME session being switched away and back where the live agent mutated messages BEFORE the switch... no wait, the cache entry is only remembered at build time (fresh from disk, unmutated), and `match` shares those instances. The risk is: hit 1 serves shared instances → live agent mutates instance X in place during its run → user switches away and back (file unchanged) → hit 2 serves the mutated X. If mutation is semantic (usage anchors — which get reset anyway by resetLoadedUsageAnchors on every load), it may benign. But other in-place mutations (ids, tool results, content) would corrupt.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-1636): auto-compaction stops dumping the internal checkpoint
  summary into the console — the default report is ONE marker line
  (`● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`); the records
  line + fenced summary moved behind the new `tui.showCompactionDetails`
  opt-in (default false), and the manual `/compact` still prints the full
  block. The headless log face no longer streams the summarizer deltas by
  default (the gh-1433 E4 live stream is part of the same opt-in; the
  gh-1430 `… reasoning` liveness line still covers the window). Nothing
  is lost — the summary stays in the session file, reachable via
  `compact_expand`.

- fix(test): gh-1732 — the `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test` sustained-contention
  validation leg spikes 3 of the 5 doubled runs per attempt instead of 4
  (CI run 39546301132, core shard 2/4: the old shape left exactly ONE
  real-wall-clock-timed doubled sample per attempt, and real jitter on
  that single sample — the very shape being modeled — inflated all three
  attempts' min ratios to a 3.30x best against the 3.2 bound while the
  real 500k growth legs on the same runner stayed green). 3-of-5 is the
  documented live-red shape ("≥3 of the 5 timed runs"): median-of-5
  [c,c,s] is still a spiked value, so the leg still proves the
  pre-gh-1532 median harness fails, and the min harness now rides two
  clean doubled samples per attempt.

- fix(#1705): CLI fresh-install boarding asks the provider choice FIRST —

## PR Description

Closes #1734
### What changed
The resumed-context cache key now carries the resume parity budget as a build `variant`, so a warm-switch hit only serves a context built under the same budget.

### Key decisions
- `ResumedContextCache.match`/`remember` accept an optional `variant` (default `0`, backward compatible); a mismatch is a clean miss, not an eviction
- `session_commands.dart` computes the budget once before the cache probe and threads it into both `match` and `remember`
- Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/cli/resumed_context_cache_test.dart   # 10 tests, incl. the new variant-miss case
```
Full `dart test`: 18 failures, all reproduced on `origin/main` (headless log/tools, backend-mode, yolo-rm, browser_ext e2e) — environment-dependent, no regressions from this change.

# gh-1734: [PERF] Session open: 6s cold boot / 12s via /sessions picker — double-paid boot, 2s context build, 4s shell boot

## Description

## Measurements (post-#1726/#1729, fa 1.0.615, goal_builder = 2.7GB JSONL)

The pathological opens are gone (was 31s+3.5min LM cap → now 70ms tail-read). What remains, measured from `~/.fah/logs/fa.log` boot_stage/resume_timing lines (2026-10-21):

**`fa --session goal_builder` — ~6s total:**
| stage | ms |
|---|---|
| session open (windowed tail-read of 2.7GB) | 70 |
| context build (estimator walk + pairing repair + image registry over the 200-record window) | ~2000 |
| process shell boot: config parse, provider catalog, MCP connect, plugins, memory store, prompt build, TUI init | ~3500-4000 (unlogged remainder) |

**`fa` then `/sessions` → goal_builder — ~12s total:** pays the ENTIRE boot stack twice — full shell boot on the default/new session (~6s), then `_switchToMetadata` re-runs the complete session lifecycle: open (66ms) + context build again (**1839ms** logged at 09:13:53) + lease release/claim + subagent rehydrate + full-history TUI replay (~2s).

## Root causes (ranked by user-visible win)

1. **Switch double-pays the boot** (`lib/src/cli/session_commands.dart` `_switchToMetadata`): config/providers/MCP/plugins/prompt are already live — only the session + its context + TUI history need rebuilding. Est. 12s → ~7s.
2. **Shell boot ~4s before first prompt**: sequential config → providers → MCP → memory → prompts → TUI. Lazy/parallel load (defer non-critical: MCP connects in background already? plugins? memory maintenance?) est. 6s → ~3-4s.
3. **Context build ~2s**: estimator walk + `validateToolPairing` + image registry over the window on EVERY open/switch. Cacheable per (session, lastRecordId) — est. → ~100ms on warm switch.

## Acceptance

- `fa --session <big>` cold start ≤ 3s on this machine (2.7GB session)
- mid-REPL `/sessions` switch to any session ≤ 2.5s (no re-boot of the shell stack; context cached or parallel)
- boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable — currently switches log only `context`
- no regression: over-window instant trim (#1726), lazy defer regime (#1729) keep their behavior + tests stay green

`resetLoadedUsageAnchors` is non-mutating — it uses `copyWith` to create new instances for assistant messages with usage, and passes everything else through as the same instance.

Now, the key correctness question: after the cached context is served, the messages (SHARED instances with the cache) get assigned to `_agent.state.messages`. During the live session, does the agent mutate Message objects in place, or does it create new ones? If the live loop mutates a message object in place (e.g., updating usage at generation time on the last assistant message), the cache's copy would be corrupted.

Note: `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` copies assistant messages with non-zero usage. On the FIRST load (fresh build), messages come from `buildContext()` — those instances get remembered in the cache via `remember(context: built)`. Wait — careful: the cache stores `built` (the original context). `match()` creates a NEW SessionContext with a fresh list but SHARED message instances.

Scenario: session S is opened at boot (fresh build) → context C1 built; messages M1..Mn are stored in cache AND used by the live agent (the same instances — `context.messages` list is used directly: `_agent.state.messages = resetLoadedUsageAnchors(messages)` — note resetLoadedUsageAnchors creates a NEW list, and copies assistant messages with usage != 0, but other messages pass through as the same instances).

So the live agent state may hold SOME of the same Message instances that the cache holds. Then user runs a prompt → does the agent mutate the last assistant message in place (stamp usage)? The doc of `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` says "the first live turn stamps fresh usage again" — how? If it mutates the AssistantMessage in place, the cached instance is mutated too.

Then a warm switch back to S (file unchanged — the file only changes when a record is appended; during the live session on ANOTHER session, S's file doesn't change) → `match()` returns the cached context with the (possibly mutated) message instances. If the live loop stamped usage into the shared instances... but wait — the live session was on a DIFFERENT session (beta), not S (alpha). The switch loaded beta's context and REPLACED `_agent.state.messages` with beta's messages. Alpha's message instances are no longer referenced by the live agent — unless the live loop held aliases (e.g., a tool result referencing a message object).

BUT: consider the SAME session being switched away and back where the live agent mutated messages BEFORE the switch... no wait, the cache entry is only remembered at build time (fresh from disk, unmutated), and `match` shares those instances. The risk is: hit 1 serves shared instances → live agent mutates instance X in place during its run → user switches away and back (file unchanged) → hit 2 serves the mutated X. If mutation is semantic (usage anchors — which get reset anyway by resetLoadedUsageAnchors on every load), it may benign. But other in-place mutations (ids, tool results, content) would corrupt.

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
# Inline comment 1 — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the scan memo grows without bound across session paths

`lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:923`:

```dart
/// Per-path last-entry memo behind [readCustomRecordsOfType]; one entry
/// per session path bounds the memory (records are small, the newest
/// scan wins).
final Map<String, _CustomRecordScanMemo> _scanMemo = {};
```

One entry **per path** does not bound the map: the process's REPL/picker can
visit an unbounded number of distinct session paths, and entries are only
ever overwritten (same path) — never evicted. Every visited session leaves a
resident `_CustomRecordScanMemo` holding its full scan result (registry
snapshots, obligations, steering, orphan reports — potentially thousands of
records on a marathon session) for the process lifetime.

The sibling cache added by this same PR got exactly the right treatment —
`ResumedContextCache` is LRU-bounded (`capacity = 4`). The scan memo should
ride the same bound, e.g. the same remove/re-insert + `while (length >
capacity)` eviction pattern, so the two memo layers degrade consistently on
long picker-heavy sessions.

The immutability contract itself checks out — I verified all current callers
(`agent_cli_steering.dart:459`, `agent_cli_persist.dart:161`,
`child_session_io.dart:57`, `session_commands.dart:795`,
`ObligationsLedger.fromPayload`) are read-only, and `CustomRecord` fields are
`final` — so this is a memory-shape concern, not a correctness one.

blocks.text:
`resetLoadedUsageAnchors` is non-mutating — it uses `copyWith` to create new instances for assistant messages with usage, and passes everything else through as the same instance.

Now, the key correctness question: after the cached context is served, the messages (SHARED instances with the cache) get assigned to `_agent.state.messages`. During the live session, does the agent mutate Message objects in place, or does it create new ones? If the live loop mutates a message object in place (e.g., updating usage at generation time on the last assistant message), the cache's copy would be corrupted.

Note: `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` copies assistant messages with non-zero usage. On the FIRST load (fresh build), messages come from `buildContext()` — those instances get remembered in the cache via `remember(context: built)`. Wait — careful: the cache stores `built` (the original context). `match()` creates a NEW SessionContext with a fresh list but SHARED message instances.

Scenario: session S is opened at boot (fresh build) → context C1 built; messages M1..Mn are stored in cache AND used by the live agent (the same instances — `context.messages` list is used directly: `_agent.state.messages = resetLoadedUsageAnchors(messages)` — note resetLoadedUsageAnchors creates a NEW list, and copies assistant messages with usage != 0, but other messages pass through as the same instances).

So the live agent state may hold SOME of the same Message instances that the cache holds. Then user runs a prompt → does the agent mutate the last assistant message in place (stamp usage)? The doc of `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` says "the first live turn stamps fresh usage again" — how? If it mutates the AssistantMessage in place, the cached instance is mutated too.

Then a warm switch back to S (file unchanged — the file only changes when a record is appended; during the live session on ANOTHER session, S's file doesn't change) → `match()` returns the cached context with the (possibly mutated) message instances. If the live loop stamped usage into the shared instances... but wait — the live session was on a DIFFERENT session (beta), not S (alpha). The switch loaded beta's context and REPLACED `_agent.state.messages` with beta's messages. Alpha's message instances are no longer referenced by the live agent — unless the live loop held aliases (e.g., a tool result referencing a message object).

BUT: consider the SAME session being switched away and back where the live agent mutated messages BEFORE the switch... no wait, the cache entry is only remembered at build time (fresh from disk, unmutated), and `match` shares those instances. The risk is: hit 1 serves shared instances → live agent mutates instance X in place during its run → user switches away and back (file unchanged) → hit 2 serves the mutated X. If mutation is semantic (usage anchors — which get reset anyway by resetLoadedUsageAnchors on every load), it may benign. But other in-place mutations (ids, tool results, content) would corrupt.

# Changelog

bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-1636): auto-compaction stops dumping the internal checkpoint
  summary into the console — the default report is ONE marker line

  attempts' min ratios to a 3.30x best against the 3.2 bound while the
  real 500k growth legs on the same runner stayed green). 3-of-5 is the
  documented live-red shape ("≥3 of the 5 timed runs"): median-of-5
  [c,c,s] is still a spiked value, so the leg still proves the

(gh-1522: the retired flow pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit
  per release). The git TAG is the single source of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` jobs. `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow

blocks.text:
`resumeParityBudget` returns an `int` — matches the `variant: int` parameter. Good.

Now, one important design question: is `budget` the RIGHT variant discriminator? The claim: "Two different budgets legitimately build different history slices — a stale-budget hit would silently serve a wrong-length context". The budget depends on:
- `_effectiveContextWindow` — could change mid-process? `/model` switch could change the window.
- `_effectiveCompactionSettings.reserveTokens` — config.
- `_agent.state.systemPrompt` — changes with mode switches! `builtInAgentModes` / `_currentMode` changes the system prompt. In `_switchToMetadata`, `_modes = builtInAgentModes(...); _currentMode = ...` happens BEFORE `_loadSession(metadata)`. So a switch from a 'code' mode session to an 'architect' mode session (different prompt → different overhead → different budget) gets a different variant → clean miss → rebuild. Correct.
- `_agent.state.tools` — tool set changes (MCP connect, plugin load) → different budget → miss. Correct.

So the variant covers the budget-dependent slice length. Good fix — this was actually pushed in commit d9f03dc0ea. Was this in response to the previous review? The review threads were about _scanMemo and CountingRangeFs only. The variant change seems to be an author-driven hardening... Actually wait, let me check the commit date again: d9f03dc0ea at 13:57:39, c219ee4efe at 13:54:23. Both before PR creation (15:18:51). So the variant was part of the initial push. Fine.

Now — the deeper question about whether the budget variant is SUFFICIENT. The context build (`buildContext`) depends on:
1. The file bytes (fingerprint covers).
2. The budget (variant covers).
3. Anything else? The compaction transform depends on the records. The `thinkingLevel`, `model` — derived from records. `activeToolNames` — from records.

Does `buildContext` depend on anything OUTSIDE the file+budget? Let me check `buildContext` in session_tree.dart. If it has hidden inputs (e.g., current time for something, or the storage's residency window state), the cache could serve stale results. The windowed open is re-done on every load (`_repo.open(metadata, windowed: true)`), and `ensureCompactionBoundaryResident(tokenBudget: budget)` pages back the same way. Then `buildContext()` projects over the resident branch. The resident branch should be deterministic given file+budget... unless `maxPages` walk hits different states. Deterministic. OK.

One more scenario for the resumed-context cache: TWO different sessions could map to the same path? No — path is the key.

What about `metadata.path` for a session whose file was ROTATED between open and switch? Rotation rewrites files (renames primary to .part-NN, creates new primary) → the primary path's stat changes (new empty file, new mtime) → miss → rebuild from the (now nearly empty primary + parts chain). But wait — would the rebuild produce the same context as before rotation? That's buildContext's concern, not the cache's. Fine.

mtimeMs granularity: on some filesystems mtime has 1s granularity (ext3) or ms (ext4). A same-second append that also keeps size identical is basically impossible (append changes size). Rotation changes sizes. Truncate+rewrite to the same size within the same millisecond — pathological, accepted risk with stat fingerprints (the whole codebase uses this pattern per the scan memo and gh design). Not a finding beyond maybe a SUGESTION... Previous review called the key "correct". Don't re-litigate.

Now — what about `_env.fileInfo` — is `ExecutionEnv.fileInfo` available on ALL backends? The fingerprint helper catches everything and returns null → no caching. Safe degradation.

Next: the `switchStage('open')` etc. — wait, `stage()` in `_loadSessionInner` logs `boot_stage $name ms=... sid=...` — and the switch adds `switchStage()` with its OWN stopwatch for rehydrate/replay. The doc says "boot_stage switch-begin/open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay/switch-done lines name the target session". `stage()` lines include sid — yes: `'boot_stage $name ms=${bootSw.elapsedMilliseconds} sid=${metadata.id}'`.

Hmm — but there's a subtlety: `stage('context source=cache')` produces `boot_stage context source=cache ms=...`. The test for the boot-stages checks `l.contains('boot_stage context') && l.contains(betaId)` — matches both `context` and `context source=cache` lines. Order test: context follows walk. Fine.

Now the parseability nit: `stage('context source=cache')` stuffs a qualifier into the stage NAME rather than a structured field. The ticket AC says "boot_stage switch lines cover every switch stage (open/walk/context/rehydrate/replay) so regressions are attributable". A log consumer parsing `boot_stage <name>` would see stage name "context source=cache" — two tokens. Minor. Could be `stage('context')` + separate `source=cache` field. That's a SUGESTION-level nit on log format. Hmm, is it worth raising? The AC's spirit is attributability; the extra token doesn't break grepping (`grep 'boot_stage context'` matches both). A strict parser expecting exactly 2 tokens after boot_stage... The prior format used single-token names. I could raise it as a SUGESTION. Let me hold it as a candidate.

Next: `_switchToMetadata` — the `cwdChanged` guard. One more scenario: `_loadAgentContext()` also matters when the SESSION's cwd is the same but the MODE changed... no, `_modes`/`_currentMode` are rebuilt unconditionally right above. Prompt overrides come from config — unchanged. Skills tree — cwd-scoped. Project context — cwd-scoped. OK.

But WAIT — one real behavior question on the same-cwd skip: `_loadAgentContext` loads skills + project context. Are there OTHER things `_loadAgentContext` does that are session-scoped or stateful (e.g., memory store per project, prompt overrides)? Let me look at `_loadAgentContext`.

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-21):
# Inline comment 1 — ⚠️ IMPORTANT: the scan memo grows without bound across session paths

`lib/src/session/session_repo.dart:923`:

```dart
/// Per-path last-entry memo behind [readCustomRecordsOfType]; one entry
/// per session path bounds the memory (records are small, the newest
/// scan wins).
final Map<String, _CustomRecordScanMemo> _scanMemo = {};
```

One entry **per path** does not bound the map: the process's REPL/picker can
visit an unbounded number of distinct session paths, and entries are only
ever overwritten (same path) — never evicted. Every visited session leaves a
resident `_CustomRecordScanMemo` holding its full scan result (registry
snapshots, obligations, steering, orphan reports — potentially thousands of
records on a marathon session) for the process lifetime.

The sibling cache added by this same PR got exactly the right treatment —
`ResumedContextCache` is LRU-bounded (`capacity = 4`). The scan memo should
ride the same bound, e.g. the same remove/re-insert + `while (length >
capacity)` eviction pattern, so the two memo layers degrade consistently on
long picker-heavy sessions.

The immutability contract itself checks out — I verified all current callers
(`agent_cli_steering.dart:459`, `agent_cli_persist.dart:161`,
`child_session_io.dart:57`, `session_commands.dart:795`,

`resetLoadedUsageAnchors` is non-mutating — it uses `copyWith` to create new instances for assistant messages with usage, and passes everything else through as the same instance.

Now, the key correctness question: after the cached context is served, the messages (SHARED instances with the cache) get assigned to `_agent.state.messages`. During the live session, does the agent mutate Message objects in place, or does it create new ones? If the live loop mutates a message object in place (e.g., updating usage at generation time on the last assistant message), the cache's copy would be corrupted.

Note: `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` copies assistant messages with non-zero usage. On the FIRST load (fresh build), messages come from `buildContext()` — those instances get remembered in the cache via `remember(context: built)`. Wait — careful: the cache stores `built` (the original context). `match()` creates a NEW SessionContext with a fresh list but SHARED message instances.

Scenario: session S is opened at boot (fresh build) → context C1 built; messages M1..Mn are stored in cache AND used by the live agent (the same instances — `context.messages` list is used directly: `_agent.state.messages = resetLoadedUsageAnchors(messages)` — note resetLoadedUsageAnchors creates a NEW list, and copies assistant messages with usage != 0, but other messages pass through as the same instances).

So the live agent state may hold SOME of the same Message instances that the cache holds. Then user runs a prompt → does the agent mutate the last assistant message in place (stamp usage)? The doc of `resetLoadedUsageAnchors` says "the first live turn stamps fresh usage again" — how? If it mutates the AssistantMessage in place, the cached instance is mutated too.

Then a warm switch back to S (file unchanged — the file only changes when a record is appended; during the live session on ANOTHER session, S's file doesn't change) → `match()` returns the cached context with the (possibly mutated) message instances. If the live loop stamped usage into the shared instances... but wait — the live session was on a DIFFERENT session (beta), not S (alpha). The switch loaded beta's context and REPLACED `_agent.state.messages` with beta's messages. Alpha's message instances are no longer referenced by the live agent — unless the live loop held aliases (e.g., a tool result referencing a message object).

BUT: consider the SAME session being switched away and back where the live agent mutated messages BEFORE the switch... no wait, the cache entry is only remembered at build time (fresh from disk, unmutated), and `match` shares those instances. The risk is: hit 1 serves shared instances → live agent mutates instance X in place during its run → user switches away and back (file unchanged) → hit 2 serves the mutated X. # Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-1636): auto-compaction stops dumping the internal checkpoint
  summary into the console — the default report is ONE marker line
  (`● auto-compacted · engine: N → M tokens (F freed · P%)`); the records
  line + fenced summary moved behind the new `tui.showCompactionDetails`
  opt-in (default false), and the manual `/compact` still prints the full
  block. The headless log face no longer streams the summarizer deltas by
  default (the gh-1433 E4 live stream is part of the same opt-in; the
  gh-1430 `… reasoning` liveness line still covers the window). Nothing
  is lost — the summary stays in the session file, reachable via
  `compact_expand`.

- fix(test): gh-1732 — the `wrap_ansi_line_perf_test` sustained-contention
  validation leg spikes 3 of the 5 doubled runs per attempt instead of 4
  (CI run 39546301132, core shard 2/4: the old shape left exactly ONE
  real-wall-clock-timed doubled sample per attempt, and real jitter on
  that single sample — the very shape being modeled — inflated all three
  attempts' min ratios to a 3.30x best against the 3.2 bound while the
  real 500k growth legs on the same runner stayed green). 3-of-5 is the
  documented live-red shape ("≥3 of the 5 timed runs"): median-of-5
  [c,c,s] is still a spiked value, so the leg still proves the
  pre-gh-1532 median harness fails, and the min harness now rides two
  clean doubled samples per attempt.

- fix(#1705): CLI fresh-install boarding asks the provider choice FIRST —
  the same list the `/add-provider` picker shows (presets, `Custom` last) —
